headline: BRIXTON HITS 142,770 g/t SILVER AT LANGIS — Highest Grades in Project History Confirm New Shallow Discovery in Ontario's Historic Cobalt Camp
snippet: Brixton Metals (TSX-V: BBB) reported the highest silver grades ever drilled at its Langis Project in Ontario's historic Cobalt silver camp, with hole LM-26-477 returning 4,164 oz/t (142,770 g/t) silver and composite hole LM-26-480 delivering 5.0 metres grading 704 g/t silver — a new shallow brownfields discovery the company identifies as structurally distinct from the deeper primary target zones. With both high-grade style and near-surface geometry confirmed, Langis emerges as one of 2026's most compelling silver exploration stories.

headline: GENESIS-VAULT GOLD MERGER EFFECTIVE TODAY — 99.74% Shareholder Vote Seals Australian Gold Consolidation; Implementation November 25
snippet: The Federal Court approved the Genesis Minerals–Vault Minerals scheme of arrangement, which became legally effective November 16 after 99.74% of votes cast at the November 11 scheme meeting supported the transaction — one of the strongest scheme votes on record for an Australian gold deal. Final implementation is set for November 25, cementing Genesis's position as a mid-tier Australian gold producer with a consolidated Western Australian asset base at a time when mid-tier M&A is accelerating globally.

headline: SELKIRK COPPER DRILLS 54,579m IN YUKON'S LARGEST-EVER COPPER PROGRAM — High-Grade Minto Results Confirm Bulk Open-Pit Potential; NI 43-101 Update Next
snippet: Selkirk Copper (TSX-V: SCMI) completed its 54,579-metre, 223-hole Phase 2 drill program at the Minto copper-gold project in Yukon Territory — the largest copper drill campaign in Yukon history — with best hole 26SCM254 returning 1.91% copper-equivalent over 9 metres within a broader 53-metre envelope at 0.83% CuEq. Management says the grades support bulk open-pit mining economics and will anchor an updated NI 43-101 resource estimate, adding a major derisking milestone at a project that sits in a district with established copper processing infrastructure.

headline: TRANSITION METALS OUTLINES 800×200m PGE-NICKEL-COPPER SYSTEM IN ONTARIO — Saturday Night Target Advances With Deep Geophysics and 3,481m of Drilling
snippet: Transition Metals (TSX-V: XTM) reported summer 2026 exploration results at its Saturday Night PGE-nickel-copper target in northern Ontario, with five diamond holes totalling 3,481 metres intersecting a mineralized envelope approximately 800 metres by 200 metres that remains open along strike and to depth. PGEs, nickel, and copper all sit on Canada's critical minerals list, adding policy tailwinds to a project now backed by both deep-penetrating geophysics and drill-confirmed mineralization.

headline: SHUTTERED PATAGONIA GOLD-SILVER MINE GETS NEW OWNER AND RESTART PLAN — Infill Drilling, Updated Resource Targeted as South American Brownfield Bet
snippet: A new ownership group announced a restart plan for a formerly producing gold-silver mine in Patagonia, targeting infill drilling and an updated resource estimate as the near-term milestones before development decisions. Brownfield restarts in Argentina and Chile's Patagonia region are attracting increasing capital in 2026 as existing infrastructure lowers per-ounce development costs relative to greenfield projects at current precious metals prices.

headline: USA RARE EARTH BOUNCES 11% AFTER Q3 MISS — First-Ever Magnet Sales Overshadowed by Feedstock Gaps; William Blair Downgrades, Jefferies Holds Buy
snippet: USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ: USAR) staged an 11% recovery after initially sinking on a Q3 earnings miss, with the volatile session illustrating the tension between its first-ever commercial rare earth magnet sales — a strategic milestone for the US domestic rare earth supply chain — and ongoing feedstock supply constraints. William Blair downgraded to Market Perform citing input shortfalls, while Jefferies maintained its Buy rating, leaving the investment case split on whether USAR's operational ramp can overcome near-term sourcing challenges.

headline: CHINA'S RARE EARTH GIANTS DOUBLE PROFITS IN 2026 — Supply Controls Drive 3.65 Billion Yuan Nine-Month Net for China Northern Rare Earth
snippet: China Northern Rare Earth and its state-backed peers more than doubled nine-month profits in 2026 as Beijing's export licensing regime tightened global supply and lifted domestic producer margins, with China Northern reporting 3.65 billion yuan (approximately US$547 million) in net profit for January–September. The gains reinforce the asymmetry between Chinese state producers — who benefit from both higher prices and preferential access to feedstock — and Western developers who face the same elevated prices for feedstock but lack integrated supply chains.

headline: CRITICAL METALS LOCKS UP 100% OF GREENLAND'S TANBREEZ — $264.5M Cash Position Sets Stage for 2027 Feasibility Push at World's Largest Known REE Deposit
snippet: Critical Metals Corp (NASDAQ: CRML) announced full ownership of the Tanbreez polymetallic-rare earth project in Greenland and a treasury of US$264.5 million in cash after completing all 2026 objectives — positioning the company to advance what it describes as the world's largest known rare earth resource into feasibility and development studies in 2027. With 100% ownership secured and a fully funded balance sheet, Critical Metals enters 2027 as one of the most capitalised pure-play rare earth developers outside China.

headline: CODELCO PARTNERS WITH ADANI FOR LONG-TERM COPPER RAW MATERIAL SUPPLY — Chile's State Miner Diversifies Buyer Base as South Asian Demand Competes With China
snippet: Chile's state copper miner Codelco has partnered with India's Adani Group to secure a long-term raw material supply arrangement, the latest in a series of strategic off-take deals as copper-intensive Indian industries compete with Chinese buyers for South American concentrate. The partnership signals Codelco's deliberate diversification of its customer base at a time when LME copper futures face financial market headwinds from AI-sector selling despite continued tightening in physical supply across both China and South Asia.

headline: WHY GOLD MINERS FALL HARDER THAN GOLD — The Structural Gap Is Now 30-40%; The Contrarian Case for Leveraged Recovery in Producer Equities
snippet: Discovery Alert's November analysis breaks down the structural reasons gold equities consistently underperform bullion in selloffs — operational leverage cuts both ways, financing costs rise with rate expectations, and institutional investors liquidate equity miners before touching physical — and argues the current 30-40% discount between mining stock valuations and spot metal prices historically precedes sharp mean reversion when the rate cycle turns. The piece identifies the cost and margin thresholds that separate overexposed producers from those best positioned for the recovery.

headline: FIVE CANADIAN GOLD MINERS TO WATCH AS EARNINGS SEASON OPENS — Stocks Near Multi-Year Valuation Lows vs. Spot Gold; Analyst Screens for Sub-$1,500 AISC
snippet: Canadian Mining Report identifies five Canadian gold producers entering Q3 earnings season with stocks at multi-year valuation lows relative to spot gold in the $3,860–$4,000 range, focusing on names with 2026 all-in sustaining cost guidance below US$1,500/oz as the highest-leverage candidates if Q4's historically strong seasonal window materialises. The screen filters out producers with balance sheet or permitting risk that could prevent them from capturing the full margin benefit of elevated gold prices.
